name: The Umami Cartographers — Synth Cuisine Collective
creator: Praxis Adeyemi-Johanssen & Seo-Yun Mwamba-Castillo
description: Founded in 2203 following the Compound Umami breakthrough, the Umami Cartographers are a collective of twelve chefs and food scientists who publish open-source 'flavor maps' — detailed neural-feed schematics showing how synthesized glutamates, tannins, and volatile aromatics can be layered to approximate or transcend real-ingredient taste profiles. Their annual 'Atlas Edition' release, distributed free on pirate neural channels, has been downloaded over 40 million times. Corporate food producers have repeatedly attempted to patent their methodologies, so far unsuccessfully.
cultural_impact: The Cartographers democratized haute cuisine technique across all tiers, enabling Shelf cooks to achieve Tier 4 flavor complexity with Φ0.30 ingredients, fundamentally destabilizing the luxury food market's claim that quality required real produce.
controversy: Axiom Workforce Solutions filed a sweeping intellectual property injunction in 2214 claiming the collective's flavor-mapping methodology derived from proprietary BCI taste-calibration patents; the case is ongoing and the collective has gone partially underground.
story_hooks: One of the twelve Cartographers has quietly sold their methodology to Axiom — and the others don't know which one.
A new Atlas Edition flavor map is circulating that doesn't match the collective's known style and contains an embedded neural payload that causes intense involuntary food memories in BCI users.
A Shelf teenager who learned to cook entirely from Cartographer maps has developed a genuinely novel flavor compound — one that the collective wants, and Axiom wants more.
